details: CONFIRMED by reading: cycle.js:284 and :290 prompts; the limits recipe (judge base "Limits"); relay_land.py Result lines for RED
("land: the gate of {branch} is red (exit {code}); log {log}", code = the gate's) and LANDED (_landed: the landed line first, then
cleanup, closed and change-record lines). The front used Bash run_in_background, which reports the real exit code; the runner has
no such tool use allowed (detached recipe), so the move to the cycle lost the code. Principle 5 (fact to code, meaning to the model):
an exit code is a fact. Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: grep -n "const prompt = " cycle.js -> 284: ... detached with the limits recipe, log ${log}. ... Report code (the exit code of relay land)
grep -n "def _landed" -A25 lib/relay_land.py -> Result(LANDED, [f"landed {branch} on {default} at ...", *lines, *closed], units)
lib/relay_land.py _locked: raise Stop(RED, [f"land: the gate of {branch} is red (exit {code}); log {log}", *red[:5]])
failing_case: The land runner follows its prompt: "run relay land <branch> -C <wt> detached with the limits recipe, log <log> ... Report code
(the exit code of relay land)". The limits recipe is `nohup <command> > <log> 2>&1 < /dev/null & echo $!`, then `kill -0` loops in
later Bash calls. A process started that way is not a child of the later shells: its exit status cannot be read, and relay land
prints no line with its exit code (on red it prints "land: the gate of X is red (exit 1); log ..." where "exit 1" is the GATE's
code; on landing "landed X on master at ..."). So `code` is what the runner model infers from the text. Example: a landing that
ends red prints the gate's own "(exit 2)" for a failing pytest step; a runner reading "exit 2" reports code 2 and the unit stops
at `land` instead of getting its land fixer. The recovery prompt (line 290, step 1) has the same gap: "report its exit code if you
can read it from its log" - the log never holds it.
Now: the branch decision of the land stage rests on a model's reading of prose. Should: the code is a fact written by the shell.
Also: `landed: first` takes the first non-blank of the LAST 5 lines; a landing that prints the cleanup output, closed items and the
change-record lines after "landed <branch> on master at <sha>" pushes that line out, so the front's merged line is built from a
cleanup line.
fix_hint: Wrap the command so the log ends with its code (`sh -c '...; echo "relay land exit $?"'`), report code from that line, in both the
land and the recovery prompt; for exit 0 report the line that starts "landed ".
pass_cases: 1. The land prompt makes the detached command write its own code: e.g. `sh -c 'relay land <b> -C <wt>; echo "relay land exit $?"'`
detached, log <log>; the prompt says to report code from the last line "relay land exit <n>". A test in
tests/test_cycle_workflow.py asserts the land runner's prompt contains that wrapper text and "relay land exit".
2. The recovery prompt's step 1 reads that same "relay land exit <n>" line from <log> (test asserts the text).
3. Exit 0 still gives {landed: <the "landed <branch> on ..." line>}: the prompt asks for the line that starts "landed " (or the
whole output), and a stub whose lines put "landed wt/x on master at abc" first among more lines gives landed = that line.
4. The existing stubbed-code tests (exit 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 2) keep their outcomes.
reason: tests/test_cycle_workflow.py test_f1_* pass at head, fail at 817cf7a6; the prompts wrap the command in sh -c with an echo of relay land exit, and read the last line.
findings.summary: the land runner is told to report relay land's exit code but nothing records it: a detached run's code is guessed from the text (principle 5)

details: CONFIRMED by reading bin/relay cmd_land (--hold branch: no rev-parse of refs/heads/<branch>) and relay_land_waits.hold/held_words
(exact match on event.branch). Branch names in this project are truncated slugs with a `wt/` prefix (this branch:
wt/the-change-cycle-script-lands-a-ready-ch for item the-change-cycle-script-lands-a-ready-change-its), so a mismatch is an
ordinary slip. The hold is the owner's word (CLAUDE.md Git: "When I say hold, wait for my word on that change"); the only new
safeguard of that word once the cycle lands by itself is this event. Size: 10 minutes.
evidence: bin/relay:697  relay_land_waits.hold(main, args[1], args[2]); print(f"{args[1]} is on hold: ...")
failing_case: The owner says "hold" on the change of item the-change-cycle-script-lands-a-ready-change-its. The front runs
`relay land --hold the-change-cycle-script-lands-a-ready-ch "hold it"` (the slug without `wt/`, or the full item slug, whose
branch name is truncated). bin/relay calls relay_land_waits.hold(main, args[1], args[2]) with no check; it prints
"the-change-... is on hold: relay land ... now exits 5". The cycle's land runner then runs `relay land wt/the-change-cycle-...`;
held_words matches event.branch exactly, finds no hold, and the branch lands. Now: the owner's hold is broken while the front was
told it holds. Should: a hold of a name that is no branch is refused, naming the next step.
fix_hint: In cmd_land (or hold()), refuse when `git rev-parse --verify -q refs/heads/<branch>` fails, listing the branches that contain the
given text; a test in tests/test_land_waits.py.
pass_cases: 1. `relay land --hold nosuch "w"` in a repo with no branch nosuch exits 2 (or the usage error code) with a line naming that no
branch nosuch exists (and the branches whose name contains it, e.g. wt/nosuch-x), and writes no hold event.
2. `relay land --hold wt/x "w"` for an existing branch wt/x writes the hold; `relay land wt/x` exits 5 (today's test still passes).
3. `relay land --release wt/x` after a hold still releases; `relay land wt/x` lands.
4. A hold on wt/a does not stop wt/b (today's test).
reason: tests/test_land_waits.py Hold::test_a_hold_on_a_name_that_is_no_branch_is_refused_and_writes_no_event passes, fails before; existing hold/release tests pass.
findings.summary: relay land --hold accepts any name: a hold on a mistyped or prefix-less branch is recorded, read by nothing, and the real branch lands

minutes plus the paid run.

failing_case: The checker's person_facing answer now decides whether a change lands without the owner. The design (5.3 c): "The checker's

section 7 budgets them. The change adds no case under evals/plugin (git diff --stat master...HEAD -- evals: nothing). Now: a checker

details: CONFIRMED by git grep -n "relay land" -- plugins: delegate/SKILL.md:130-136 and :213-219 unchanged by the change. The change must
touch it to keep its promise (the front lands nothing the cycle landed). The brief limits files to what the design names; this
file is a caller the design missed. Size: 5 minutes.
evidence: plugins/delegate/skills/delegate/SKILL.md:136 `built` takes `built`. It does not land a change: the merge is the
plugins/delegate/skills/delegate/SKILL.md:213 8. **Take the default branch.** The front's `relay land` takes it
failing_case: The front reads the delegate skill when it starts the cycle. It says (line 136) "It does not land a change: the merge is the
front's." and step 8 (line 213) "The front's `relay land` takes it"; the unit fields list has no `land`, and the settings land,
land_fixes, land_reruns are not named. The front skill now says the opposite ("The cycle lands a ready change itself ... start no
relay land"). Now: two texts the front loads disagree on who lands; a front that follows the delegate skill starts a second relay
land for a unit the cycle already landed or is landing (it waits for the lock, then is refused or lands nothing), or does not know
how to keep a unit from landing (land: false). Should: the delegate skill says the cycle lands in relay mode and names the field
and settings.
fix_hint: Edit the two passages and the unit-field line.
pass_cases: 1. plugins/delegate/skills/delegate/SKILL.md no longer contains "It does not land a change"; it says that in relay mode the cycle

2. The unit fields line names `land`; the settings land, land_fixes, land_reruns are named where the skill names the cycle's args.
3. Step 8 says the cycle's land stage (or the front, for a unit stopped at land) runs relay land.
findings.summary: the delegate skill still says the cycle does not land a change and that the front's relay land takes the default branch

details: CONFIRMED by reading bin/paid-cost main ("touches": return 1 on no default branch and on GitError; return 0 if files else 1) and
relay_land_waits.touches_paid_paths. Rare today (the branch exists after preflight), hence LOW. Size: 10 minutes.
evidence: bin/paid-cost: print("paid-cost: the default branch cannot be told"); return 1 ... except GitError: return 1 ... return 0 if files else 1
failing_case: touches_paid_paths returns `returncode == 0`. bin/paid-cost touches exits 1 both for "no file on the paid paths" and for "the
default branch cannot be told" or a git error, and python exits 2 when the script cannot be opened. Example: a git diff error of
`refs/heads/master...wt/x` during a going paid run gives exit 1 -> False -> check() returns -> the branch lands. Should: an error
stops the landing (refused or exit 6), never lets it through.
fix_hint: Give touches an error exit of 2 and treat anything but 0/1 as a refusal.
pass_cases: 1. touches exits with a distinct code (e.g. 2) on an error, and touches_paid_paths raises Stop(REFUSED, ["land: cannot tell whether
<b> touches the paid paths: <stderr>"]) for it; a test stubs PAID_COST to a script that exits 2.
2. A branch touching only lib/ in a going run still lands (today's test).
3. A branch touching plugins/ in a going run still exits 6 (today's test).
findings.summary: an error of bin/paid-cost touches reads as 'touches no paid path', so a failure lands a paid-path branch during a paid run

details: PLAUSIBLE (no second relay-mode project yet). The owner's answer was to "which of relay's own texts count". Size: 5 minutes.

details: PLAUSIBLE: depends on how bin/eval-record separates "not judged" from "a case failed" (ci prints one message for both). The landing
outcome for ordinary branches is the same (exit 6); only the --paid-fix way is wrong. Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: lib/relay_paid.py:172-173 if not judge(data): return State(RED, ...)
plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md "Not judged (money ceiling, runs not judged, the day's cap): the waiting changes keep waiting"
failing_case: A paid run on master whose money ceiling trips writes an eval record that is not green (partial). state() returns RED: "the paid
run begun <ts> was red", and relay land's exit 6 line adds "the fix item lands with relay land <b> --paid-fix". The front skill
says a not-judged run has no fix item: "the waiting changes keep waiting; run again on the same head". A front that follows the
line lands an unrelated branch with --paid-fix. Should: a not-judged record gives its own line (run again on the same head) and
--paid-fix is refused for it.
fix_hint: Read the reason from bin/eval-record and give a NOT_JUDGED state, or word the RED line to cover both.
pass_cases: 1. An eval record that bin/eval-record judges "not judged" (the ceiling or unjudged runs) gives a state whose line says to run the
paid run again on the same head; --paid-fix is refused in it; paid-path branches exit 6.
2. A record with a case that failed its majority stays RED with the --paid-fix line (today's test).
reason: tests/test_land_waits.py Paid::test_a_record_that_was_not_judged_is_not_red_and_paid_fix_is_refused and tests/test_relay_paid.py State tests pass, fail before.
findings.summary: a run that was not judged (money ceiling, day's cap mid-run) is reported as red with the --paid-fix way, which the front skill gives only to a fix item
